- Overestimate prices in the short term (1-3 days) after sentiment spikes (positive sentiment > 0.3), especially when recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (sentiment < 0.1) and recent prices are trending down — model tends to ignore downward pressure.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +0.5+ in 1-2 days) — model reacts too aggressively, then corrects too late.
- Mean-reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to adjust downward when sentiment turns negative or price consolidates.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate by 0.5–1.5% in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive — adjust downward by 0.2–0.4% for first 7 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.2–0.4), model overfits recent noise — reduce forecast sensitivity to short-term sentiment swings.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is flat or slightly declining, model overestimates — reduce forecast by 0.3–0.6% to avoid “sentiment-driven overreach.”
